faq.answer: No. Conflict, competition, attraction norms, trauma history, or unequal power may intensify expression. Use matched topics and consent-aware comparisons.
faq.question: Does intense expression establish One-to-one Type Four?

faq.answer: A close person may welcome, tolerate, or fear intensity, and power can limit refusal. Recording limits prevents coercion from becoming a subtype example.
faq.question: Why must consent be recorded in a focal comparison?

faq.answer: Intensity explained by objective stakes, stable expression across audiences, or reliable de-escalation after a clear limit should weaken it.
faq.question: What weakens the focal-intensity hypothesis?

sections.body_md: The description proposes that Type Four difference attention may concentrate around a specific person or rivalry. It is not a claim that intensity causes attachment.
sections.title: Treat focal intensity as a traditional hypothesis

sections.body_md: Compare the same disagreement or creative challenge with a close person, neutral collaborator, and anonymous evaluator. Record intensity, evidence, consent, repair, and stakes.
sections.title: Match the topic while changing the focal person

sections.body_md: The label organizes focal attention, comparison, and intensity. It is not evidence about bodily mechanisms, chemistry, sexuality, or a force determining attraction.
sections.title: Keep one-to-one language non-mechanistic

sections.body_md: Difference may appear as challenging another person, outperforming a rival, or demanding unmistakable engagement. Compare this with real competition and unsafe conflict.
sections.title: Allow competition to carry difference concerns

sections.body_md: Relationship conflict, competitive fields, trauma history, cultural scripts, harassment, and evaluation power can intensify expression. Consent and safety are mandatory context.
sections.title: Test conflict, power, and attraction norms

sections.body_md: The hypothesis weakens when intensity follows objective stakes rather than focal identity, remains stable across audiences, or reliably decreases when another person sets a limit.
sections.title: Use neutral response and respected limits as tests

sections.body_md: Results from one measure remain context-bound. This page cannot predict attraction, conflict, compatibility, creativity, or relationship quality.
sections.title: Keep focal observations non-predictive

Duration: 5

Context: Use the same disagreement or creative challenge with a close person, neutral collaborator, and anonymous evaluator.

Observable signal: Record topic, stakes, evidence, intensity, consent, limit, evaluation power, repair, and change after refusal.

Page-specific signal: Compare whether the same evidence produces different intensity only when a particular relationship or rivalry is present.

Alternative explanation: Compare conflict, competition, trauma history, cultural scripts, harassment, attraction norms, and power.

Reflection prompt: Identify the condition where stakes or safety explain intensity better than subtype and cite one respected limit.

seo.description: One-to-one Type Four is a traditional, evidence-limited hypothesis that identity-and-meaning attention may appear through focal comparison, intensity, and testing whether a specific relationship can hold difference. Intense expression cannot establish subtype because conflict, attraction norms, trauma history, competition, and unequal power can look similar.
seo.title: One-to-one Type Four: focal intensity as a matched-comparison hypothesis
